correctness.rationale: The 12 line equations in Z[omega] give precisely nine fourfold intersections and twelve double points, independently enumerated from all 66 pairs by the attached exact checker. Resolution gives 21 vertices and 48 nodes (genus 28). The complete integral Laplacian is [[5I-C,-B],[-B^T,4I]], with B^TB=3I+J and BB^T=2I+J-C. Its eigenvalues are \(0^1,3^{11},7^9\). The matrix-tree formula fixes order \(3^{10}7^8\). The rank of the full Laplacian is 10 modulo 3 and 12 modulo 7, proved via Schur complement 21I-3H-J and independently checked by exact arithmetic. Therefore all primary elementary divisors have exponent one, giving \((\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z)^2\oplus(\mathbb Z/21\mathbb Z)^8\). The graph-to-Néron identification is conditional on unit-thickness regular split semistability. The checker independently reproduces geometry, spectrum, determinant, and integer Smith form.

value.rationale: The canonical stable Hesse boundary uses all twelve inflection lines and resolves exactly the nine non-nodal points, so the component-group question is intrinsic to a classical geometric degeneration. The previously computed Hesse incidence-only graph has no 7-primary part; the twelve ordinary triangle nodes change the actual integral degeneration pairing and create eight independent 7-primary factors. The two-eigenvalue Laplacian structure and exact prime-local rank argument explain the result, rather than an arbitrary numerical Smith calculation. The exact invariant can be used for Jacobian degeneration component groups under natural unit-thickness smoothings; no larger downstream theorem is asserted.
